title: Switzer's 29-0-1 Start Ended by Kansas in 1975
question: How long was Barry Switzer's unbeaten start at Oklahoma and who ended it?
answer: Barry Switzer opened his Oklahoma career 29-0-1, with a 7-7 tie at USC in 1973 as the only blemish. Kansas ended it with a 23-3 upset in Norman on November 8, 1975, and Oklahoma still won the national title.
summary: Barry Switzer started 29-0-1 at Oklahoma, including a 28-game win streak, until Kansas won 23-3 in Norman on Nov. 8, 1975. The Sooners still took the title.
body: When Barry Switzer took over the Sooners in 1973, few coaches in the country have ever begun a tenure better. His first team went 10-0-1, and the lone blemish was a 7-7 tie at top-ranked USC on September 29. That Sooner side also blanked Nebraska 27-0 along the way.
The 1974 team went 11-0 and is recognized as a national champion. By the time the 1975 season opened, Switzer's record at Oklahoma stood at 21-0-1.

The 1975 Sooners kept it going, opening 8-0 and arriving at the Kansas game ranked No. 2. Along the way they beat Texas 24-17 in Dallas and won at Oklahoma State. Switzer's start reached 29-0-1, which Sports Illustrated also frames as a 28-game winning streak, counted from the game after the USC tie.

Then came November 8, 1975. Kansas visited Norman and won 23-3, with a blocked punt and three Sooner turnovers helping the Jayhawks. It was Oklahoma's first loss since mid-October 1972, and Switzer's first as head coach.

The sting did not last. Oklahoma beat Missouri 28-27 and Nebraska 35-10, clinched the Big Eight title, and then topped Michigan 14-6 in the Orange Bowl to repeat as national champions. Fans still count the Kansas game as the rare slip in one of the great opening runs in college football.
